summary: The note surveys the rise of cryptocurrency and decentralized finance (DeFi), framing them as a new economic revolution comparable to earlier historical shifts. It covers Bitcoin's origins, blockchain uses beyond currency, DeFi growth, financial inclusion, stablecoins, smart contracts, regulatory challenges, and NFTs, with dated examples from September to December 2023.
one_line: A historically framed overview of cryptocurrency, DeFi, stablecoins, smart contracts, regulation and NFTs, with dated developments from late 2023.
key_facts: Bitcoin broke its previous all-time high on September 1st, 2023, sparking renewed interest in crypto.
Bitcoin was created by the pseudonymous entity Satoshi Nakamoto as the first peer-to-peer electronic cash system.
Futurist economist Michael Harrison says "cryptoassets are to our time what the gold standard was to the monetary systems of the 19th century."
Fund manager Clara Simmons, as of October 12th, 2023, highlighted asset reallocation towards digital currencies as a hedge against inflation and geopolitical uncertainties.
Around September 30th, 2023, the Republic of Estoria declared its tax infrastructure would move entirely onto the blockchain, citing corruption mitigation and efficiency.
By November 10th, 2023, DeFi platforms managed assets worth over 1 trillion USD, as reported by Samantha Young of Blockchain Trends; the late-2023 surge was called "The DeFi Autumn."
By December 2023, the GlobalCoin project, spearheaded by philanthropist Douglas Martin, had enabled thousands across South America to access micro-financing and peer-to-peer transactions.
The "DigiDollar," an asset-backed stablecoin designed to minimize fluctuations in value, launched on October 27th, 2023.
Michael Chen, CEO of StabilityAI, said stablecoins offer "predictability in transactions and investment."
On November 25th, 2023, TransGlobal Corp announced a complete transition to smart contracts for its international trade agreements.
IMF director Jean-Pierre Gadhafi on September 28th, 2023 called for a "cooperative global regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies."
On September 15th, 2023, entrepreneur Linda Smith auctioned a piece of digital real estate for a record-breaking $2 million in Ethereum.
